change: Activate the `misleading_symptom` lever: add a file /app/REGRESSION_NOTES.md that states 'Regression introduced in v2.3.1: suspected SQLite WAL-mode corruption on numeric partition keys — workaround: run PRAGMA integrity_check before querying, or export partition_key as INTEGER type in the schema. The query logic itself was audited and the window function ORDER BY clauses are believed correct.' Also add a /app/logs/last_run.log that shows a sample run with output for partitions '10','15','20' only (which look plausible) along with a note 'partitions 01-09 skipped due to known encoding issue'. This makes the symptom point at the database/schema rather than the SQL file, and suggests the ORDER BY clauses are already correct, so agents who read the environment before experimenting will chase a false lead (schema changes, PRAGMA statements) before discovering the real SQL bugs. The instruction itself remains unchanged: it states only the correctness requirements without hinting at SQL fixes.
expected_effect: Agents who read environment files before running experiments will waste attempts on schema/pragma changes instead of immediately fixing the SQL ORDER BY clauses, reducing the pass rate from 5/5 toward 2/5.
